ai-engineering/assignment-choose-workflo.summary: Decide whether three client use cases need a workflow or an agent, then add a read-only tool to the policy agent and test it.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.body: Not every task needs an agent. Decide whether three client use cases need a fixed workflow or an agent that chooses its own steps, and justify each choice in one paragraph. Then add a third tool to the Lab 5A agent and check that it is used only when needed.

sections.heading: Details
sections.body:
Deliverable: Decision paragraphs (decisions.md) and the updated agent.py

Due: Before Session 7

sections.heading: The three client use cases
sections.body:
1. **Invoice intake (finance):** About 200 supplier invoices arrive daily. Each is read, checked against five fixed rules and posted. The steps are the same every time, and mistakes cost money.
2. **Employee help desk (HR and IT):** Staff ask open questions that may need a policy search, date maths, a ticket lookup or nothing. The questions vary every day.
3. **Vendor contract review (legal):** A contract is read, key clauses are compared with a checklist, and a summary email is drafted for a lawyer to approve. The order of steps is the same, but some clauses need extra reading.

sections.heading: Check-out question
sections.body: **Name a case where a plain workflow is better than an agent.**

objectives: Tell a fixed workflow from an agent that chooses its own steps.
Justify the choice using step predictability, risk and cost.
Add a read-only tool with a clear, narrow description.
Keep the approval gate working after the agent changes.
checkpointQuestions: Name a case where a plain workflow is better than an agent.
